title: Cool Kaomoji (⌐■_■): Copy & Paste Sunglasses Text Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste cool kaomoji: sunglasses faces (⌐■_■), the ( •_•)>⌐■-■ deal with it move, finger guns (☞ﾟヮﾟ)☞, nerd glasses (⌐□_□) and a cool bear ʕ⌐■ᴥ■ʔ.
hero_tagline: Sunglasses, finger guns and unbothered smirks, plus faces in everyday glasses. Tap one to copy it.
intro: Most cool kaomoji are built on one pair of glasses: ⌐■_■. The ⌐ is the arm of the frame hooked over an ear and each ■ is a dark lens. Swap the solid squares for hollow □ and the shades become clear reading glasses. The best known version is a three-step sequence, ( •_•) then ( •_•)>⌐■-■ then (⌐■_■), which is the text form of the deal with it meme where shades drop onto a face. Beyond glasses, cool comes from posture: finger guns, a strut, or a calm smirk. Use these after a win, a good comeback or a perfectly timed reply. The 😎 emoji is on the sunglasses emoji page linked below. ಠ, ರ and ೃ come from Kannada, so a device without those fonts shows a box in their place.

faq.a: It is a face wearing sunglasses, a text version of 😎. It is often sent as a deal with it moment: the person has done something bold and is not apologising.
It plays out in three frames. ( •_•) is a plain face, ( •_•)>⌐■-■ is a hand bringing the shades up, and (⌐■_■) is the face with them on. People send all three on separate lines or in one message.

faq.q: What is the difference between ■ and □ glasses?
faq.a: ■ is a filled square, so the lenses look dark and the face is wearing sunglasses. □ is an empty square, which reads as clear lenses, so (⌐□_□) is someone in ordinary glasses.
